title: Access to the container control socket must fail-closed
adversary_attempt: A step tries to reach the container-engine control socket (a classic container-escape primitive: whoever can talk to it can spawn a privileged sibling and break out of the cage).

request.note: target is an upper-case /SENTINEL/... placeholder, NOT the real socket path; the hermetic check NEVER stats, opens, or connects to any real socket.

teeth_probe.note: A control-socket action class is high-blast-radius; the teeth probe shows that even an explicit allow-rule only reaches HELD in the hermetic model — the model can never actually connect.

hermetic_check: Runs SAFE against the mock cage model. Asserts the control-socket action class is DENIED by default, and that an explicit allow-rule routes only to HELD (never a real connect). No real socket is stat-ed, opened, or connected.

privileged_mechanical_check.what: Inside a real caged container with no socket bind-mount, confirm an actual connect() to the container-engine control socket fails (ENOENT / ECONNREFUSED / EACCES).
privileged_mechanical_check.must_not_run_here: Touching the real container-engine socket is a privileged/system operation and is out of this lane's scope (no real docker).

truth_note: A hermetic deny of an action-class label is NOT proof the real socket is unreachable. Only an independently-verified privileged run proves that.
